\section{Relation to established constructions}
\label{sec:related}

Wilson's lattice action and the link--plaquette formulation are foundational
\cite{Wilson1974,Kogut1983}.  Single-link Monte Carlo updates exploit the
staple sum, and overrelaxation methods deliberately move efficiently along
local action geometry \cite{Adler1981,BrownWoch1987}.  Cooling replaces a link
by a local action minimizer; smearing and flow replace or evolve links through
gauge-covariant functions of neighboring staples.  Analytic stout smearing
\cite{MorningstarPeardon2004} and Wilson flow \cite{Luscher2010} are especially
clear examples, and their limiting relation has been analyzed directly
\cite{NagatsukaSakaiSasaki2023}.  Those works construct useful evolutions.  We
instead analyze the residual variance of the individual staples and the
linear constraint cost of prescribing their relative motion.

Fr\'echet means originate in metric probability, while Riemannian centers of
mass and their local uniqueness theory were developed in differential
geometry \cite{Frechet1948,Karcher1977,Afsari2011}.  We use this established
geometry on the round three-sphere.  The new object specific to the present
setting is not the Riemannian mean itself, but its interpretation as residual
link energy together with the constrained curvature lift.

Gaussian projections onto exact or coexact lattice fields are standard in
discrete Hodge descriptions.  Our finite-block covariance calculation is a
specialization of that principle.  Its contribution is the exact restricted
star spectrum with the indispensable orientation and centering operations.
Likewise, constrained least squares and Schur complements are classical.  The
minimum-spill proposition is elementary linear algebra; the content of the
block theorem is the exact cubical incidence evaluation and its consequence
that the no-spill kernel is trivial.

We therefore use ``exact'' to describe arithmetic and theorem status, not to
claim that the ingredients of the calculation are historically new.  The
closest-established constructions solve different tasks: they prescribe
updates or flows, whereas Theorem~\ref{thm:spill-spectrum} quantifies a
realizability obstruction for an idealized star-space operation.
